title: Pageflow shim for blocked KV coalescing and GPU page stabilizer
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Under continuous batching workloads we observe repeated small-slot evictions for KV entries that oscillate between host and GPU memory. This causes token-latency spikes and increases GPU swap bandwidth. Goal: Implement a compact, low-latency 'pageflow shim' that groups logical KV slots into aligned block windows, applies conservative coalescing for contiguous-hot runs, and introduces a GPU-side page stabilizer to reduce thrashing during workload waves.

Scope: prototype an allocator shim in the runtime that maps KV keys into 'pageflow blocks' (configurable block size in entries) and maintains a light-weight per-block residency score. Integrate with the existing paging coordinator to: 1) bias prefetches to whole-block candidates for recent-access wavefronts; 2) delay demotions of blocks below a hysteresis threshold to avoid oscillation; and 3) expose backpressure signals to the batching layer when host swap bandwidth exceeds a soft limit.

Design details: 
- Block layout: A pageflow block groups N contiguous logical KV slots (default N=64). Block metadata is a compact header per block (8 bytes): residency_bitmap (bitmap compressed), last_access_epoch, hot_score_age, and a backoff counter.
- Residency policy: Blocks are demoted/promoted atomically. We avoid per-slot LRU to reduce bookkeeping cost and atomic contention under high concurrency.
- Prefetch strategy: Two-tier prefetching: (A) conservative block prefetch for the top-K recent blocks based on hot_score_age, (B) speculative single-slot prefetch for tail-of-batch predicted next-token affinity. The conservative path uses DMA-friendly, aligned transfers.
- GPU page stabilizer: A soft pinning mechanism that marks blocks as 'stabilized' for a short epoch window after being promoted. Stabilized blocks are exempt from eviction unless forced by a critical OOM signal. The stabilizer also smooths eviction order by adding a tunable decay to hot_score_age.
- Backpressure and batching coordination: The shim exposes a single backpressure metric (host_swap_bytes_per_sec) and a boolean overload flag. When overload is true, the batching controller reduces max batch size and increases latency SLO window for affected routes to lower swap pressure.
- Observability: add per-block counters and histograms for swap latency, contiguous-transfer size, and stabilization hold-time. Add dashboards and an SLI for swap-induced tail latency (>99p token delay).

Trade-offs considered: 
- Larger block sizes reduce metadata and transfer overhead but increase wasted prefetch for sparse access patterns. We set defaults conservatively and add runtime per-model tuning.
- Atomic block promotions simplify correctness but can delay fine-grained eviction of rarely used slots. We mitigate by allowing speculative single-slot demote candidates when memory pressure is extreme.
- Pinning reduces thrash but risks long-lived GPU residency; we use short stabilization epochs and reactive demotion on sustained pressure.

Acceptance criteria: 
- End-to-end 99th-token latency reduction by >=20% on sampled production mix with continuous batching enabled.
- Swap bandwidth reduction by >=25% for same mix.
- No regression (>1%) in average throughput on heavy short-context workloads.

Rollout plan: 
1) Canary prototype on staging with synthetic wavefront workload (week 1).
2) Small customer canary (1-2 tenants) with telemetry gates and kill-switch (week 2).
3) Gradual ramp to 25% traffic with metric-based rollback conditions (week 3).

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Mis-tuned block size causes increased host traffic. Mitigation: runtime feature flags per-deployment and auto-tune module to observe access sparsity.
- Risk: Cross-AI-model variance. Mitigation: per-model profiles and default-off for models that report dense KV hotsets.

Next steps: finalize shim API, implement block header pack/unpack, add unit tests for atomic promote/demote paths, and prepare perf harness.
updates: 2026-02-16: Spike completed to measure average contiguous access runs across production traces. Observed median run-length=12 slots, 95p=72 slots.
2026-02-20: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Agreed on 64-slot default block and two-tier prefetch. Action: produce API sketch for promote/demote calls (Diego).
2026-02-25: Prototype allocator shim implemented: block mapping and header placement. Microbenchmarks: atomic promote cost ~120ns, contiguous transfer overhead reduced by 18% vs per-slot transfers.
2026-03-01: Integration test added with batch controller backpressure hook. Observed swap bandwidth reduction in synthetic workload by 30% when stabilization epoch=2s.
2026-03-05: Submitted RFC PR #1124 for in-team review. Seeking security review for potential impacts on KMS/HSM codepaths (stabilizer pin metadata visibility).
